subject: forensic-medicine
title: Infanticide and child abuse: live birth tests, fetal death signs and abuse syndromes

steps.tx: **Infanticide** means the killing of a child after birth, up to one year of age. In India it is tried as murder under section 302 IPC, so the prosecution must prove the child was born alive and then killed. A child is legally presumed born dead until proven otherwise. Viability is the ability to live separately from the mother, reached at about 210 days (7 months, 28 weeks) of gestation.

steps.tx: Crying alone does not prove live birth, because a child may cry in the uterus or vagina (**vagitus uterinus** or **vagitus vaginalis**) and still be born without life. Signs of live birth include muscular movements, sneezing and yawning. Proof of live birth in court usually depends on postmortem findings and the tests below.

steps.tx: The **hydrostatic test**, also called Raygat's test, depends on lungs floating after respiration, since a respired lung has a lower specific gravity than water. Breslau's second life test checks for swallowed air in the stomach and intestine. Wredin's test finds air in the middle ear, and Ploucquet's test finds the lung weight to body weight ratio rising from about 1/70 to 1/35.

steps.tx: Each test has false results. Hydrostatic test false negatives occur in **atelectasis**, pulmonary oedema, pneumonia and congenital syphilis, where a respired lung may sink. False positives occur in putrefaction and attempted artificial respiration. Gettler's test is not a live birth test; it measures chloride difference between heart chambers to suggest antemortem drowning.

steps.tx: A **dead born** child shows rigor mortis, maceration, putrefaction or mummification after complete birth. In maceration, skin slippage appears first, around 12 hours, and **Robert's sign** (gas in the great vessels and heart) follows. **Spalding's sign**, overriding of skull bones, appears about a week after death and is the classic sign of maceration.

steps.tx: Child abuse includes **battered baby syndrome**, where multiple fractures at different healing stages, subdural haematoma and retinal bleeding appear without a matching history. **Shaken baby syndrome** causes subdural haemorrhage and retinal haemorrhage. **Munchausen syndrome by proxy** is a carer fabricating illness in the child. **Sudden infant death syndrome** is an unexplained death in infancy, after a postmortem excludes other causes.
